✨ The Names by Florence Knapp (2025) ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Literary)

🖤 Three-Fifths by John Vercher (2025) ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Historical Fiction/1995)

😂 The Guncle by Steven Rowley (2022) ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Contemporary)

🧩 The Strange Case of Jane O. by Karen Thompson Walker (2025) ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Mystery)

💙 Blue Sisters by Coco Mellors (2024) ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Contemporary/Family Drama)

🥰❤️🥰❤️🥰❤️🥰
My Favorite: This batch of five is filled with books that grabbed me for completely different reasons. The Names by Florence Knapp blew me away with its smart, literary look at identity, memory, and the stories that shape us—it felt like the kind of novel I want to underline on every page. Three-Fifths by John Vercher was a gut punch in the best way: raw, tense, and deeply human as it explores race, secrets, and 1995 Pittsburgh. For something lighter, The Guncle by Steven Rowley was pure joy—heartfelt, funny, and unexpectedly emotional, with characters you just want to hug. The Strange Case of Jane O. hooked me immediately with its eerie atmosphere and twisty mystery that had me guessing until the end. And Blue Sisters by Coco Mellors delivered a gorgeously messy, emotional family drama full of complicated relationships, grief, and beautifully flawed characters. Five very different books, all memorable for their own reasons. 💛📚

Yet another sushi review 🍣🍱🪩what can I say, I love 🐠. Took a break from our full-time job (aka CS40) with my fav @ashleyjeonn to eat at @genkiya_sushi in Davis Square (they have locations all around the Boston area). The ambiance is nice and very calm, especially on a weeknight. The service was incredible- our server was super nice and quick! We ordered the Makimono combo to share, which had 24 pieces of sushi: tuna, salmon, spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, and california rolls. They all tasted fresh- I will say, the spicy tuna specifically isn’t my favorite here. It could definitely be more flavorful and I wish it was wrapped in a little more rice. My favorite was the shrimp tempura roll because of the crunch and the yummy sauce on top. Overall, Genki Ya is solid! Not my all-time favorite sushi spot in the area, but it’s reliable and a nice place to sit down. 

Food: 7.5/10

At the time of this trip, I only needed 16 more restaurants to complete the Hamburger America book.  Three of those were in New Jersey.  Thanks to my buddy Joe doing the driving and planning, we knocked off all three.  First up was Krug’s Tavern in Newark.  This was a hectic area and I was quite pleased I wasn’t doing the driving.  We each ordered our own bacon cheeseburgers, which come with a side of fries.  These burgers are big boys, weighing in uncooked at 12 ozs.  The loose texture reminds me of the steamed cheeseburgers of Meriden, CT.  They use fresh ground meat from a local butcher and there is obviously magic on that grill.  This is one of the most flavorful burgers in the book and all three of us were blown away.  It just doesn’t get any better than this.  Unaware that fries would be coming with the burgers, I also ordered a side of sweet potato fries, which also were a revelation.  We also split an Italian dog just for the novelty.  Cool old bar atmosphere with smiling, friendly service, Krug’s Tavern is a gem!  #krugstavern  #roadfoodnewjersey #roadfood #newarkeats #newarkfood #newarkburgers #cheeseburger #baconcheeseburger #since1932 #maritonshamburgeramericatour

Jay-Z’s “Girls, Girls, Girls” carries more hidden history than most fans realize. Producer Just Blaze once revealed that Michael Jackson secretly recorded background vocals for the remix, though they were never released. Even more surprising, the beat wasn’t originally destined for Jay-Z-Kanye West, Ghostface Killah, and Snoop Dogg all passed on it before it landed on The Blueprint. The track also features uncredited vocals from Q-Tip, Slick Rick, and Biz Markie, adding layers of hip-hop royalty to the mix. Built on a soulful sample from Tom Brock’s “There’s Nothing in This World That Can Stop Me From Loving You” and interpolations of Crash Crew’s “High Power Rap,” the record was made in April 2001, just months before Jay was in Los Angeles shooting the video when the tragic events of September 11 unfolded.

Would you believe me if I told you that delicious award-winning whiskey is being produced in Newark, New Jersey?  Well, it’s true.  Yesterday, I sat down with All Points West Distillery’s founder and partner Gil Spaier for a tasting and Q&A. 

I particularly enjoyed the @allpointswestdistillery “Malt and Grain Pot Still Whiskey” that is mashed, fermented, pot distilled, and aged under a single roof on Tichenor Street in Newark.  Interestingly, the Irish formerly pot distilled their whiskey with corn, but this was deemed “too American” and discontinued.  APWD brings back the corn in this expression, resulting in a delicious whiskey reminiscent of Redbreast, but with a long finish and a pronounced chocolate note on the back end.

This whiskey is the perfect star for the Tipperary Cocktail (invented in 1916 by NYC bartender Hugo Ensslin). I tweaked the recipe as shown below - it’s a delicious and well-balanced spirit-forward cocktail.  Sip it slowly and enjoy!

2 oz. All Points West Malt and Grain Pot Still Whiskey
½ oz sweet vermouth 
¼ oz Green Chartreuse
2 dashes of Angostura bitters

Combine ingredients in a mixing glass.  Add ice and stir.  Strain into a chilled coupe glass.  Express a lemon twist over the drink (optional) - discard lemon twist.

Tonight we stopped by Portucale, a restaurant specializing in traditional Portugese fare with a focus on fish and seafood dishes. We started with the PotuCale sampler including pulpo and camarones al ajillo, fried Spanish potatoes, and Portugese chourico. The octopus was perfectly tender and well-seasoned, and the shrimp had great salinity that balanced nicely with a squeeze of lemon. Both dishes had a tasty garlic oil that was perfect for dipping. For my main, I ordered the cataplana de mariscos, a seafood stew bearing the name of the traditional double clam shell cookware from the Algarve region that it is cooked in. The cataplana included lobster, crab, clams, mussels, shrimp, and scallops in a rich tomato, white wine based broth. This dish transported us right back to southern Portugal, perfectly cooked seafood, a delicious broth enhanced by the natural brine of the shellfish, and tender vegetables to complement every bite. 

Our second main included butterflied and grilled seabass seasoned with fried garlic and vegetables. The seabass had perfect sear on the skin side and tender flesh with great flavor, as usual the Portuguese really know how to grill fish without drying it out. We wrapped up our meal with an espresso and passionfruit mousse, the mousse had a fresh passionfruit topping that brought an impressive amount of tanginess and balance to the dish. In addition to a flavorful dessert, nothing punctuates a good meal like a warm goodbye from restaurant staff.

Among ethnic groups that landed in New World to call America home, Italians have brought the recipes that evolved into the independent branch of Italian-American cuisine, where ..a bit bigger is beautiful, red sauce and plentiful cheese dominates and “cucina povera” is a memory. Just look at New York pizzas.. And then Greeks got trapped in the nostalgia of home ending up recycling the same recipes into more and more blunt tzatziki and moussaka. But the Portuguese got excited with the sea bounty of this side of the ocean, into more ingredients beyond the cod they have exploited for years. Seafood, clams, octopuses and fish were more abundant, bigger and plenty-full, to be cooked in Portuguese fashion that transforms in a simple, yet meaningful way any subpar ingredient into a bite full of ocean flavor.. So when we realized that Unc (@chef_jes1 ) had a son, who is a cultural icon, we had to pay homage. See, Newark is a town about that fish sandwich and hoops. 27 years ago, I died. Figuratively. Everything changed in an instant. And from that day forward this is the new birth date. 

There are no coincidences when you are in control. Only signs. And for us the sign has been on, the grind has been nonstop. The Black Excellence, unapologetically. The alley-oops. The Community. The Chase of Freedom. 

If you are what you eat, and you have chosen to share that meal with us, you are now the culmination of a culture that has built this nation, this city, and our community with a LOVE and JOY that is pure. Eternally grateful and thankful.

So much of our culture doesn’t get the access and opportunity to shine. He gave us time on his hard earned platform to get our offerings out to the world in a way we couldn’t, hadn’t, and who knows if we would have without him. The new world places us a unique crossroad and we have to decide where, how, and why the CULTURE should choose our path. Like this Brother, we are choosing the path of EXCELLENCE and JOY. 

So, in his honor and to thank him, we do what we do: the JUPITER JAWN. Our call and response to the cheesesteak. Freshly shaved ribeye. Chopped in the flat top in oxtail fat. Grilled onions. Cooper sharp American cheese. Hit with the oxtail jus. Topped with our oxtail gravy. Drizzle of our Masala Sauce from @burgerwalla ! We are thankful.

We don’t make high end food. It’s not art. The plating sucks. We got more of our techniques from watching Yan Can Cook and trying to understand Jacques Pepin than from staging in our whites. Our ethos is heavy on Bourdain and at all times trying to hey approval from our Grandmommas. 

But students learn, and the culture must be protected and uplifted at ALL times. Integrity matters. Being thoughtful matters. 

So when @asmalls777 walked into @theyardnewark with @lindajbaraka on Monday, our off day and when I come in to clean do the “job” parts of this story…you have to consider what you’re doing, how you’re doing it, and why you chose this life. He is undoubtedly one of the stewards of our culture, unapologetically Black and uncompromising in our commitment to excellence. We have an integrity to maintain and uplift, and our means of this moment is Black Culinary Culture. 

While he didn’t get to eat (which later had me in damn near tears!!!), it was another sign that we are doing things the right way. That integrity matters. And the CULTURE in and of itself is the purest form of art in this crazy world. So yes, we sell this food but we do so consciously. 

Amari Baraka said, “Art is a weapon in the struggle of ideas, the class struggle.” He also said, “The artist’s role is to raise the consciousness of the People. To make them understand life, the world, and themselves more completely.”

Some times you can get all of that from burger n fries, in a Black & Fun spot, that preaches Joy. I guess there’s an art in that.

Bottom-Up vs. Top-Down Treatment for Headaches

https://DrEricChiropractorOnline.com/1782/bottom-up-vs-top-down-treatment-for-headaches/

Because each case is unique and headaches can have multiple underlying or contributing causes (they can also co-occur), the authors note that the ideal bottom-up/top-down treatments will depend on the doctor’s clinical reasoning and experience. That is, there is no one size fits all. For example, there are several studies showing that migraine headache patients may experience reduced headache frequency and intensity after receiving manual therapies to address trigger points in their cervical muscles (a bottom-up approach).

The authors conclude that a multi-modal approach may be the most effective way to manage migraine, tension-type, cervicogenic, and other types of headaches. Such an approach may include spinal manipulation, spinal mobilization (non-thrust), soft-tissue therapies (massage, trigger point therapy, stretching, myofascial release), needling (wet & dry needling of trigger points and/or acupuncture), general exercise, targeted exercise, and cognitive interventions.

Most chiropractors embrace and utilize all or at least many of these non-drug treatment strategies when managing patients with headaches, though they may co-manage with other healthcare providers if necessary.

Four Whiplash Myths

https://DrEricChiropractorOnline.com/1798/four-whiplash-myths/

Myth #1: Whiplash Is Only Caused By Rear-End Automobile Collisions. Although most WAD injuries are associated with this mechanism, impacts from other directions can also lead to whiplash injuries, as can a slip and fall, sports collision, or even a physical altercation.

Myth #2: Low-Speed “Fender Benders” Don’t Cause Whiplash. It does NOT take a lot of force to become injured. Studies have demonstrated that a collision as slow as 5-10 mph can cause bodily harm. This is partly because modern vehicles are designed to crumple and absorb energy during more forceful impacts. In a low-speed crash, these forces can be transferred to the occupants of the car.

Myth #3: There’s No Rush to See a Doctor. It’s very common for people to delay seeking treatment if it’s not an emergency and if they feel like taking time off work to make a doctor appointment might be more inconvenient than their aches and pains. Or they might think they can self-manage the condition with over-the-counter medications or home remedies. However, in most instances, WAD will not go away on its own, and delaying care can actually increase the risk that one develops chronic WAD.

Myth #4: Recovery from Whiplash Requires a Lot of Rest. Years ago, treatment recommendations emphasized bed rest and a cervical collar. However, the current research supports the opposite approach: continue your normal daily activities as much as possible. Excessive rest and immobilization can weaken tissues, especially cartilage that requires movement to receive nutrients.

Here’s the bottom line: If you’re involved in a car crash or another form of serious collision, get checked out by a healthcare provider as soon as possible. Doctors of chiropractic are a great option, and studies support that early intervention with manual therapies and other forms of conservative care can effectively manage most acute WAD symptoms and reduce the risk for chronicity.

Another linoblock cut I did while in college. I was pretty obsessed with Picasso when I was a kid. He was one of many artists my Mom hipped me 2. Unbeknownst to me and my Mother, we had no clue of the nuances of what cultural appropriation was all about. In fact we didn’t have any knowledge of how white supremacy played a roll in what my Mother and I saw in gallery’s and museums. 

With all of that said, my Mother was simply trying to give me what would be my 1st lessons in art education. 

Both original Lino blocks are very much connected to my Mother. She was the one who 1st made a connection with my love for art and artists like Picasso. My Mom did show me Basquiat and when I showed an interest in collages, Jacob Lawrence was her 1st go to. 
.
I miss my parents deeply and my art is directly connected to their legacy. As Father’s Day approaches, I will definitely tell some stories about him.
